      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.pl\"\n  - \"**/*.pm\"\n  - \"**/*.t\"\n  - \"**/*.psgi\"\n  - \"**/*.cgi\"\n---\n> This file extends common/hooks.md with Perl-specific content.\nConfigure in :\n**perltidy**: Auto-format  and  files after edit\n**perlcritic**: Run lint check after editing  files\nWarn about  in non-script  files ",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.pl\"\n  - \"**/*.pm\"\n  - \"**/*.t\"\n  - \"**/*.psgi\"\n  - \"**/*.cgi\"\n---\n# Perl Hooks\n\n> This file extends [common/hooks.md](../common/hooks.md) with Perl-specific content.\n\n## PostToolUse Hooks\n\nConfigure in `~/.claude/settings.json`:\n\n- **perltidy**: Auto-format `.pl` and `.pm` files after edit\n- **perlcritic**: Run lint check after editing `.pm` files\n\n## Warnings\n\n- Warn about `print` in non-script `.pm` files — use `say` or a logging module (e.g., `Log::Any`)\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.pl&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/<em>.pm&quot;\n  - &quot;**/<\/em>.t&quot;\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.psgi&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/*.cgi&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>Perl Hooks<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/hooks.md\">common/hooks.md<\/a> with Perl-specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>PostToolUse Hooks<\/h2>\n<p>Configure in <code>~/.claude/settings.json<\/code>:<\/p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>perltidy<\/strong>: Auto-format <code>.pl<\/code> and <code>.pm<\/code> files after edit<\/li>\n<li><strong>perlcritic<\/strong>: Run lint check after editing <code>.pm<\/code> files<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Warnings<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Warn about <code>print<\/code> in non-script <code>.pm<\/code> files — use <code>say<\/code> or a logging module (e.g., <code>Log::Any<\/code>)<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n"

      "type": "rule",

      "path": "rules/perl/patterns.md",
      "title": "Perl Patterns",
      "description": "--- paths:   - \"**/*.pl\"   - \"**/*.pm\"   - \"**/*.t\"   - \"**/*.psgi\"   - \"**/*.cgi\" --- > This file extends common/patter",
      "metadata": {},
      "risks": [],
      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.pl\"\n  - \"**/*.pm\"\n  - \"**/*.t\"\n  - \"**/*.psgi\"\n  - \"**/*.cgi\"\n---\n> This file extends common/patterns.md with Perl-specific content.\nUse **DBI** or **DBIx::Class** behind an interface:\nUse **Moo** classes with **Types::Standard** (equivalent to Python dataclasses):\nAlways use **",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.pl\"\n  - \"**/*.pm\"\n  - \"**/*.t\"\n  - \"**/*.psgi\"\n  - \"**/*.cgi\"\n---\n# Perl Patterns\n\n> This file extends [common/patterns.md](../common/patterns.md) with Perl-specific content.\n\n## Repository Pattern\n\nUse **DBI** or **DBIx::Class** behind an interface:\n\n```perl\npackage MyApp::Repo::User;\nuse Moo;\n\nhas dbh => (is => 'ro', required => 1);\n\nsub find_by_id ($self, $id) {\n    my $sth = $self->dbh->prepare('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?');\n    $sth->execute($id);\n    return $sth->fetchrow_hashref;\n}\n```\n\n## DTOs / Value Objects\n\nUse **Moo** classes with **Types::Standard** (equivalent to Python dataclasses):\n\n```perl\npackage MyApp::DTO::User;\nuse Moo;\nuse Types::Standard qw(Str Int);\n\nhas name  => (is => 'ro', isa => Str, required => 1);\nhas email => (is => 'ro', isa => Str, required => 1);\nhas age   => (is => 'ro', isa => Int);\n```\n\n## Resource Management\n\n- Always use **three-arg open** with `autodie`\n- Use **Path::Tiny** for file operations\n\n```perl\nuse autodie;\nuse Path::Tiny;\n\nmy $content = path('config.json')->slurp_utf8;\n```\n\n## Module Interface\n\nUse `Exporter 'import'` with `@EXPORT_OK` — never `@EXPORT`:\n\n```perl\nuse Exporter 'import';\nour @EXPORT_OK = qw(parse_config validate_input);\n```\n\n## Dependency Management\n\nUse **cpanfile** + **carton** for reproducible installs:\n\n```bash\ncarton install\ncarton exec prove -lr t/\n```\n\n## Reference\n\nSee skill: `perl-patterns` for comprehensive modern Perl patterns and idioms.\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.pl&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/<em>.pm&quot;\n  - &quot;**/<\/em>.t&quot;\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.psgi&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/*.cgi&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>Perl Patterns<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/patterns.md\">common/patterns.md<\/a> with Perl-specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>Repository Pattern<\/h2>\n<p>Use <strong>DBI<\/strong> or <strong>DBIx::Class<\/strong> behind an interface:<\/p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-perl\">package MyApp::Repo::User;\nuse Moo;\n\nhas dbh =&gt; (is =&gt; &#39;ro&#39;, required =&gt; 1);\n\nsub find_by_id ($self, $id) {\n    my $sth = $self-&gt;dbh-&gt;prepare(&#39;SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?&#39;);\n    $sth-&gt;execute($id);\n    return $sth-&gt;fetchrow_hashref;\n}\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>DTOs / Value Objects<\/h2>\n<p>Use <strong>Moo<\/strong> classes with <strong>Types::Standard<\/strong> (equivalent to Python dataclasses):<\/p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-perl\">package MyApp::DTO::User;\nuse Moo;\nuse Types::Standard qw(Str Int);\n\nhas name  =&gt; (is =&gt; &#39;ro&#39;, isa =&gt; Str, required =&gt; 1);\nhas email =&gt; (is =&gt; &#39;ro&#39;, isa =&gt; Str, required =&gt; 1);\nhas age   =&gt; (is =&gt; &#39;ro&#39;, isa =&gt; Int);\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Resource Management<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Always use <strong>three-arg open<\/strong> with <code>autodie<\/code><\/li>\n<li>Use <strong>Path::Tiny<\/strong> for file operations<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<pre><code class=\"language-perl\">use autodie;\nuse Path::Tiny;\n\nmy $content = path(&#39;config.json&#39;)-&gt;slurp_utf8;\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Module Interface<\/h2>\n<p>Use <code>Exporter &#39;import&#39;<\/code> with <code>@EXPORT_OK<\/code> — never <code>@EXPORT<\/code>:<\/p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-perl\">use Exporter &#39;import&#39;;\nour @EXPORT_OK = qw(parse_config validate_input);\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Dependency Management<\/h2>\n<p>Use <strong>cpanfile<\/strong> + <strong>carton<\/strong> for reproducible installs:<\/p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">carton install\ncarton exec prove -lr t/\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Reference<\/h2>\n<p>See skill: <code>perl-patterns<\/code> for comprehensive modern Perl patterns and idioms.<\/p>\n"
    },

      "type": "rule",
      "subtype": "rule_md",
      "path": "rules/perl/security.md",
      "title": "Perl Security",
      "description": "--- paths:   - \"**/*.pl\"   - \"**/*.pm\"   - \"**/*.t\"   - \"**/*.psgi\"   - \"**/*.cgi\" --- > This file extends common/securi",
      "metadata": {},
      "risks": [],
      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.pl\"\n  - \"**/*.pm\"\n  - \"**/*.t\"\n  - \"**/*.psgi\"\n  - \"**/*.cgi\"\n---\n> This file extends common/security.md with Perl-specific content.\nUse  flag on all CGI/web-facing scripts\nSanitize  (, , etc.) before any external command\nUse allowlist regex for untainting — never \nValidate all ",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.pl\"\n  - \"**/*.pm\"\n  - \"**/*.t\"\n  - \"**/*.psgi\"\n  - \"**/*.cgi\"\n---\n# Perl Security\n\n> This file extends [common/security.md](../common/security.md) with Perl-specific content.\n\n## Taint Mode\n\n- Use `-T` flag on all CGI/web-facing scripts\n- Sanitize `%ENV` (`$ENV{PATH}`, `$ENV{CDPATH}`, etc.) before any external command\n\n## Input Validation\n\n- Use allowlist regex for untainting — never `/(.*)/s`\n- Validate all user input with explicit patterns:\n\n```perl\nif ($input =~ /\\A([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)\\z/) {\n    my $clean = $1;\n}\n```\n\n## File I/O\n\n- **Three-arg open only** — never two-arg open\n- Prevent path traversal with `Cwd::realpath`:\n\n```perl\nuse Cwd 'realpath';\nmy $safe_path = realpath($user_path);\ndie \"Path traversal\" unless $safe_path =~ m{\\A/allowed/directory/};\n```\n\n## Process Execution\n\n- Use **list-form `system()`** — never single-string form\n- Use **IPC::Run3** for capturing output\n- Never use backticks with variable interpolation\n\n```perl\nsystem('grep', '-r', $pattern, $directory);  # safe\n```\n\n## SQL Injection Prevention\n\nAlways use DBI placeholders — never interpolate into SQL:\n\n```perl\nmy $sth = $dbh->prepare('SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?');\n$sth->execute($email);\n```\n\n## Security Scanning\n\nRun **perlcritic** with the security theme at severity 4+:\n\n```bash\nperlcritic --severity 4 --theme security lib/\n```\n\n## Reference\n\nSee skill: `perl-security` for comprehensive Perl security patterns, taint mode, and safe I/O.\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.pl&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/<em>.pm&quot;\n  - &quot;**/<\/em>.t&quot;\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.psgi&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/*.cgi&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>Perl Security<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/security.md\">common/security.md<\/a> with Perl-specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>Taint Mode<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Use <code>-T<\/code> flag on all CGI/web-facing scripts<\/li>\n<li>Sanitize <code>%ENV<\/code> (<code>$ENV{PATH}<\/code>, <code>$ENV{CDPATH}<\/code>, etc.) before any external command<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Input Validation<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Use allowlist regex for untainting — never <code>/(.*)/s<\/code><\/li>\n<li>Validate all user input with explicit patterns:<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<pre><code class=\"language-perl\">if ($input =~ /\\A([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)\\z/) {\n    my $clean = $1;\n}\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>File I/O<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Three-arg open only<\/strong> — never two-arg open<\/li>\n<li>Prevent path traversal with <code>Cwd::realpath<\/code>:<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<pre><code class=\"language-perl\">use Cwd &#39;realpath&#39;;\nmy $safe_path = realpath($user_path);\ndie &quot;Path traversal&quot; unless $safe_path =~ m{\\A/allowed/directory/};\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Process Execution<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Use <strong>list-form <code>system()<\/code><\/strong> — never single-string form<\/li>\n<li>Use <strong>IPC::Run3<\/strong> for capturing output<\/li>\n<li>Never use backticks with variable interpolation<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<pre><code class=\"language-perl\">system(&#39;grep&#39;, &#39;-r&#39;, $pattern, $directory);  # safe\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>SQL Injection Prevention<\/h2>\n<p>Always use DBI placeholders — never interpolate into SQL:<\/p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-perl\">my $sth = $dbh-&gt;prepare(&#39;SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?&#39;);\n$sth-&gt;execute($email);\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Security Scanning<\/h2>\n<p>Run <strong>perlcritic<\/strong> with the security theme at severity 4+:<\/p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">perlcritic --severity 4 --theme security lib/\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Reference<\/h2>\n<p>See skill: <code>perl-security<\/code> for comprehensive Perl security patterns, taint mode, and safe I/O.<\/p>\n"
    },

      "type": "rule",
      "subtype": "rule_md",
      "path": "rules/perl/testing.md",
      "title": "Perl Testing",
      "description": "--- paths:   - \"**/*.pl\"   - \"**/*.pm\"   - \"**/*.t\"   - \"**/*.psgi\"   - \"**/*.cgi\" --- > This file extends common/testin",
      "metadata": {},
      "risks": [],
      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.pl\"\n  - \"**/*.pm\"\n  - \"**/*.t\"\n  - \"**/*.psgi\"\n  - \"**/*.cgi\"\n---\n> This file extends common/testing.md with Perl-specific content.\nUse **Test2::V0** for new projects (not Test::More):\nAlways use  to ensure  is on .\nUse **Devel::Cover** — target 80%+:\n**Test::MockModule** — mock",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.pl\"\n  - \"**/*.pm\"\n  - \"**/*.t\"\n  - \"**/*.psgi\"\n  - \"**/*.cgi\"\n---\n# Perl Testing\n\n> This file extends [common/testing.md](../common/testing.md) with Perl-specific content.\n\n## Framework\n\nUse **Test2::V0** for new projects (not Test::More):\n\n```perl\nuse Test2::V0;\n\nis($result, 42, 'answer is correct');\n\ndone_testing;\n```\n\n## Runner\n\n```bash\nprove -l t/              # adds lib/ to @INC\nprove -lr -j8 t/         # recursive, 8 parallel jobs\n```\n\nAlways use `-l` to ensure `lib/` is on `@INC`.\n\n## Coverage\n\nUse **Devel::Cover** — target 80%+:\n\n```bash\ncover -test\n```\n\n## Mocking\n\n- **Test::MockModule** — mock methods on existing modules\n- **Test::MockObject** — create test doubles from scratch\n\n## Pitfalls\n\n- Always end test files with `done_testing`\n- Never forget the `-l` flag with `prove`\n\n## Reference\n\nSee skill: `perl-testing` for detailed Perl TDD patterns with Test2::V0, prove, and Devel::Cover.\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.pl&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/<em>.pm&quot;\n  - &quot;**/<\/em>.t&quot;\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.psgi&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/*.cgi&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>Perl Testing<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/testing.md\">common/testing.md<\/a> with Perl-specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>Framework<\/h2>\n<p>Use <strong>Test2::V0<\/strong> for new projects (not Test::More):<\/p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-perl\">use Test2::V0;\n\nis($result, 42, &#39;answer is correct&#39;);\n\ndone_testing;\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Runner<\/h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">prove -l t/              # adds lib/ to @INC\nprove -lr -j8 t/         # recursive, 8 parallel jobs\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<p>Always use <code>-l<\/code> to ensure <code>lib/<\/code> is on <code>@INC<\/code>.<\/p>\n<h2>Coverage<\/h2>\n<p>Use <strong>Devel::Cover<\/strong> — target 80%+:<\/p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">cover -test\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Mocking<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Test::MockModule<\/strong> — mock methods on existing modules<\/li>\n<li><strong>Test::MockObject<\/strong> — create test doubles from scratch<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Pitfalls<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Always end test files with <code>done_testing<\/code><\/li>\n<li>Never forget the <code>-l<\/code> flag with <code>prove<\/code><\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Reference<\/h2>\n<p>See skill: <code>perl-testing<\/code> for detailed Perl TDD patterns with Test2::V0, prove, and Devel::Cover.<\/p>\n"
    },
    {
      "type": "rule",
      "subtype": "rule_md",
      "path": "rules/php/coding-style.md",
      "title": "PHP Coding Style",
      "description": "--- paths:   - \"**/*.php\"   - \"**/composer.json\" --- > This file extends common/coding-style.md with PHP specific conten",
      "metadata": {},
      "risks": [],
      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.php\"\n  - \"**/composer.json\"\n---\n> This file extends common/coding-style.md with PHP specific content.\nFollow **PSR-12** formatting and naming conventions.\nPrefer  in application code.\nUse scalar type hints, return types, and typed properties everywhere new code permits.\nPrefer i",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.php\"\n  - \"**/composer.json\"\n---\n# PHP Coding Style\n\n> This file extends [common/coding-style.md](../common/coding-style.md) with PHP specific content.\n\n## Standards\n\n- Follow **PSR-12** formatting and naming conventions.\n- Prefer `declare(strict_types=1);` in application code.\n- Use scalar type hints, return types, and typed properties everywhere new code permits.\n\n## Immutability\n\n- Prefer immutable DTOs and value objects for data crossing service boundaries.\n- Use `readonly` properties or immutable constructors for request/response payloads where possible.\n- Keep arrays for simple maps; promote business-critical structures into explicit classes.\n\n## Formatting\n\n- Use **PHP-CS-Fixer** or **Laravel Pint** for formatting.\n- Use **PHPStan** or **Psalm** for static analysis.\n- Keep Composer scripts checked in so the same commands run locally and in CI.\n\n## Imports\n\n- Add `use` statements for all referenced classes, interfaces, and traits.\n- Avoid relying on the global namespace unless the project explicitly prefers fully qualified names.\n\n## Error Handling\n\n- Throw exceptions for exceptional states; avoid returning `false`/`null` as hidden error channels in new code.\n- Convert framework/request input into validated DTOs before it reaches domain logic.\n\n## Reference\n\nSee skill: `backend-patterns` for broader service/repository layering guidance.\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.php&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/composer.json&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>PHP Coding Style<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/coding-style.md\">common/coding-style.md<\/a> with PHP specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>Standards<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Follow <strong>PSR-12<\/strong> formatting and naming conventions.<\/li>\n<li>Prefer <code>declare(strict_types=1);<\/code> in application code.<\/li>\n<li>Use scalar type hints, return types, and typed properties everywhere new code permits.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Immutability<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Prefer immutable DTOs and value objects for data crossing service boundaries.<\/li>\n<li>Use <code>readonly<\/code> properties or immutable constructors for request/response payloads where possible.<\/li>\n<li>Keep arrays for simple maps; promote business-critical structures into explicit classes.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Formatting<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Use <strong>PHP-CS-Fixer<\/strong> or <strong>Laravel Pint<\/strong> for formatting.<\/li>\n<li>Use <strong>PHPStan<\/strong> or <strong>Psalm<\/strong> for static analysis.<\/li>\n<li>Keep Composer scripts checked in so the same commands run locally and in CI.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Imports<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Add <code>use<\/code> statements for all referenced classes, interfaces, and traits.<\/li>\n<li>Avoid relying on the global namespace unless the project explicitly prefers fully qualified names.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Error Handling<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Throw exceptions for exceptional states; avoid returning <code>false<\/code>/<code>null<\/code> as hidden error channels in new code.<\/li>\n<li>Convert framework/request input into validated DTOs before it reaches domain logic.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Reference<\/h2>\n<p>See skill: <code>backend-patterns<\/code> for broader service/repository layering guidance.<\/p>\n"
    },
    {
      "type": "rule",
      "subtype": "rule_md",
      "path": "rules/php/hooks.md",
      "title": "PHP Hooks",
      "description": "--- paths:   - \"**/*.php\"   - \"**/composer.json\"   - \"**/phpstan.neon\"   - \"**/phpstan.neon.dist\"   - \"**/psalm.xml\" ---",
      "metadata": {},
      "risks": [],
      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.php\"\n  - \"**/composer.json\"\n  - \"**/phpstan.neon\"\n  - \"**/phpstan.neon.dist\"\n  - \"**/psalm.xml\"\n---\n> This file extends common/hooks.md with PHP specific content.\nConfigure in :\n**Pint / PHP-CS-Fixer**: Auto-format edited  files.\n**PHPStan / Psalm**: Run static analysis after PH",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.php\"\n  - \"**/composer.json\"\n  - \"**/phpstan.neon\"\n  - \"**/phpstan.neon.dist\"\n  - \"**/psalm.xml\"\n---\n# PHP Hooks\n\n> This file extends [common/hooks.md](../common/hooks.md) with PHP specific content.\n\n## PostToolUse Hooks\n\nConfigure in `~/.claude/settings.json`:\n\n- **Pint / PHP-CS-Fixer**: Auto-format edited `.php` files.\n- **PHPStan / Psalm**: Run static analysis after PHP edits in typed codebases.\n- **PHPUnit / Pest**: Run targeted tests for touched files or modules when edits affect behavior.\n\n## Warnings\n\n- Warn on `var_dump`, `dd`, `dump`, or `die()` left in edited files.\n- Warn when edited PHP files add raw SQL or disable CSRF/session protections.\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.php&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/composer.json&quot;\n  - &quot;<strong>/phpstan.neon&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/phpstan.neon.dist&quot;\n  - &quot;**/psalm.xml&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>PHP Hooks<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/hooks.md\">common/hooks.md<\/a> with PHP specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>PostToolUse Hooks<\/h2>\n<p>Configure in <code>~/.claude/settings.json<\/code>:<\/p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Pint / PHP-CS-Fixer<\/strong>: Auto-format edited <code>.php<\/code> files.<\/li>\n<li><strong>PHPStan / Psalm<\/strong>: Run static analysis after PHP edits in typed codebases.<\/li>\n<li><strong>PHPUnit / Pest<\/strong>: Run targeted tests for touched files or modules when edits affect behavior.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Warnings<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Warn on <code>var_dump<\/code>, <code>dd<\/code>, <code>dump<\/code>, or <code>die()<\/code> left in edited files.<\/li>\n<li>Warn when edited PHP files add raw SQL or disable CSRF/session protections.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n"
    },

      "risks": [],
      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.php\"\n  - \"**/composer.json\"\n---\n> This file extends common/patterns.md with PHP specific content.\nKeep controllers focused on transport: auth, validation, serialization, status codes.\nMove business rules into application/domain services that are easy to test without HTTP bootstr",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.php\"\n  - \"**/composer.json\"\n---\n# PHP Patterns\n\n> This file extends [common/patterns.md](../common/patterns.md) with PHP specific content.\n\n## Thin Controllers, Explicit Services\n\n- Keep controllers focused on transport: auth, validation, serialization, status codes.\n- Move business rules into application/domain services that are easy to test without HTTP bootstrapping.\n\n## DTOs and Value Objects\n\n- Replace shape-heavy associative arrays with DTOs for requests, commands, and external API payloads.\n- Use value objects for money, identifiers, date ranges, and other constrained concepts.\n\n## Dependency Injection\n\n- Depend on interfaces or narrow service contracts, not framework globals.\n- Pass collaborators through constructors so services are testable without service-locator lookups.\n\n## Boundaries\n\n- Isolate ORM models from domain decisions when the model layer is doing more than persistence.\n- Wrap third-party SDKs behind small adapters so the rest of the codebase depends on your contract, not theirs.\n\n## Reference\n\nSee skill: `api-design` for endpoint conventions and response-shape guidance.\nSee skill: `laravel-patterns` for Laravel-specific architecture guidance.\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.php&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/composer.json&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>PHP Patterns<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/patterns.md\">common/patterns.md<\/a> with PHP specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>Thin Controllers, Explicit Services<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Keep controllers focused on transport: auth, validation, serialization, status codes.<\/li>\n<li>Move business rules into application/domain services that are easy to test without HTTP bootstrapping.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>DTOs and Value Objects<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Replace shape-heavy associative arrays with DTOs for requests, commands, and external API payloads.<\/li>\n<li>Use value objects for money, identifiers, date ranges, and other constrained concepts.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Dependency Injection<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Depend on interfaces or narrow service contracts, not framework globals.<\/li>\n<li>Pass collaborators through constructors so services are testable without service-locator lookups.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Boundaries<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Isolate ORM models from domain decisions when the model layer is doing more than persistence.<\/li>\n<li>Wrap third-party SDKs behind small adapters so the rest of the codebase depends on your contract, not theirs.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Reference<\/h2>\n<p>See skill: <code>api-design<\/code> for endpoint conventions and response-shape guidance.\nSee skill: <code>laravel-patterns<\/code> for Laravel-specific architecture guidance.<\/p>\n"
    },
    {
      "type": "rule",
      "subtype": "rule_md",
      "path": "rules/php/security.md",
      "title": "PHP Security",
      "description": "--- paths:   - \"**/*.php\"   - \"**/composer.lock\"   - \"**/composer.json\" --- > This file extends common/security.md with ",
      "metadata": {},
      "risks": [],
      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.php\"\n  - \"**/composer.lock\"\n  - \"**/composer.json\"\n---\n> This file extends common/security.md with PHP specific content.\nValidate request input at the framework boundary (, Symfony Validator, or explicit DTO validation).\nEscape output in templates by default; treat raw HTML rend",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.php\"\n  - \"**/composer.lock\"\n  - \"**/composer.json\"\n---\n# PHP Security\n\n> This file extends [common/security.md](../common/security.md) with PHP specific content.\n\n## Input and Output\n\n- Validate request input at the framework boundary (`FormRequest`, Symfony Validator, or explicit DTO validation).\n- Escape output in templates by default; treat raw HTML rendering as an exception that must be justified.\n- Never trust query params, cookies, headers, or uploaded file metadata without validation.\n\n## Database Safety\n\n- Use prepared statements (`PDO`, Doctrine, Eloquent query builder) for all dynamic queries.\n- Avoid string-building SQL in controllers/views.\n- Scope ORM mass-assignment carefully and whitelist writable fields.\n\n## Secrets and Dependencies\n\n- Load secrets from environment variables or a secret manager, never from committed config files.\n- Run `composer audit` in CI and review new package maintainer trust before adding dependencies.\n- Pin major versions deliberately and remove abandoned packages quickly.\n\n## Auth and Session Safety\n\n- Use `password_hash()` / `password_verify()` for password storage.\n- Regenerate session identifiers after authentication and privilege changes.\n- Enforce CSRF protection on state-changing web requests.\n\n## Reference\n\nSee skill: `laravel-security` for Laravel-specific security guidance.\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.php&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/composer.lock&quot;\n  - &quot;**/composer.json&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>PHP Security<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/security.md\">common/security.md<\/a> with PHP specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>Input and Output<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Validate request input at the framework boundary (<code>FormRequest<\/code>, Symfony Validator, or explicit DTO validation).<\/li>\n<li>Escape output in templates by default; treat raw HTML rendering as an exception that must be justified.<\/li>\n<li>Never trust query params, cookies, headers, or uploaded file metadata without validation.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Database Safety<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Use prepared statements (<code>PDO<\/code>, Doctrine, Eloquent query builder) for all dynamic queries.<\/li>\n<li>Avoid string-building SQL in controllers/views.<\/li>\n<li>Scope ORM mass-assignment carefully and whitelist writable fields.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Secrets and Dependencies<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Load secrets from environment variables or a secret manager, never from committed config files.<\/li>\n<li>Run <code>composer audit<\/code> in CI and review new package maintainer trust before adding dependencies.<\/li>\n<li>Pin major versions deliberately and remove abandoned packages quickly.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Auth and Session Safety<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Use <code>password_hash()<\/code> / <code>password_verify()<\/code> for password storage.<\/li>\n<li>Regenerate session identifiers after authentication and privilege changes.<\/li>\n<li>Enforce CSRF protection on state-changing web requests.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Reference<\/h2>\n<p>See skill: <code>laravel-security<\/code> for Laravel-specific security guidance.<\/p>\n"
    },

      "title": "PHP Testing",
      "description": "--- paths:   - \"**/*.php\"   - \"**/phpunit.xml\"   - \"**/phpunit.xml.dist\"   - \"**/composer.json\" --- > This file extends ",
      "metadata": {},
      "risks": [],
      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.php\"\n  - \"**/phpunit.xml\"\n  - \"**/phpunit.xml.dist\"\n  - \"**/composer.json\"\n---\n> This file extends common/testing.md with PHP specific content.\nUse **PHPUnit** as the default test framework. If **Pest** is configured in the project, prefer Pest for new tests and avoid mixing fra",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.php\"\n  - \"**/phpunit.xml\"\n  - \"**/phpunit.xml.dist\"\n  - \"**/composer.json\"\n---\n# PHP Testing\n\n> This file extends [common/testing.md](../common/testing.md) with PHP specific content.\n\n## Framework\n\nUse **PHPUnit** as the default test framework. If **Pest** is configured in the project, prefer Pest for new tests and avoid mixing frameworks.\n\n## Coverage\n\n```bash\nvendor/bin/phpunit --coverage-text\n# or\nvendor/bin/pest --coverage\n```\n\nPrefer **pcov** or **Xdebug** in CI, and keep coverage thresholds in CI rather than as tribal knowledge.\n\n## Test Organization\n\n- Separate fast unit tests from framework/database integration tests.\n- Use factory/builders for fixtures instead of large hand-written arrays.\n- Keep HTTP/controller tests focused on transport and validation; move business rules into service-level tests.\n\n## Inertia\n\nIf the project uses Inertia.js, prefer `assertInertia` with `AssertableInertia` to verify component names and props instead of raw JSON assertions.\n\n## Reference\n\nSee skill: `tdd-workflow` for the repo-wide RED -> GREEN -> REFACTOR loop.\nSee skill: `laravel-tdd` for Laravel-specific testing patterns (PHPUnit and Pest).\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.php&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/phpunit.xml&quot;\n  - &quot;<strong>/phpunit.xml.dist&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/composer.json&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>PHP Testing<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/testing.md\">common/testing.md<\/a> with PHP specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>Framework<\/h2>\n<p>Use <strong>PHPUnit<\/strong> as the default test framework. If <strong>Pest<\/strong> is configured in the project, prefer Pest for new tests and avoid mixing frameworks.<\/p>\n<h2>Coverage<\/h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">vendor/bin/phpunit --coverage-text\n# or\nvendor/bin/pest --coverage\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<p>Prefer <strong>pcov<\/strong> or <strong>Xdebug<\/strong> in CI, and keep coverage thresholds in CI rather than as tribal knowledge.<\/p>\n<h2>Test Organization<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Separate fast unit tests from framework/database integration tests.<\/li>\n<li>Use factory/builders for fixtures instead of large hand-written arrays.<\/li>\n<li>Keep HTTP/controller tests focused on transport and validation; move business rules into service-level tests.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Inertia<\/h2>\n<p>If the project uses Inertia.js, prefer <code>assertInertia<\/code> with <code>AssertableInertia<\/code> to verify component names and props instead of raw JSON assertions.<\/p>\n<h2>Reference<\/h2>\n<p>See skill: <code>tdd-workflow<\/code> for the repo-wide RED -&gt; GREEN -&gt; REFACTOR loop.\nSee skill: <code>laravel-tdd<\/code> for Laravel-specific testing patterns (PHPUnit and Pest).<\/p>\n"
    },

      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.py\"\n  - \"**/*.pyi\"\n---\n> This file extends common/coding-style.md with Python specific content.\nFollow **PEP 8** conventions\nUse **type annotations** on all function signatures\nPrefer immutable data structures:\n**black** for code formatting\n**isort** for import sorting\n**ruff** ",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.py\"\n  - \"**/*.pyi\"\n---\n# Python Coding Style\n\n> This file extends [common/coding-style.md](../common/coding-style.md) with Python specific content.\n\n## Standards\n\n- Follow **PEP 8** conventions\n- Use **type annotations** on all function signatures\n\n## Immutability\n\nPrefer immutable data structures:\n\n```python\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass User:\n    name: str\n    email: str\n\nfrom typing import NamedTuple\n\nclass Point(NamedTuple):\n    x: float\n    y: float\n```\n\n## Formatting\n\n- **black** for code formatting\n- **isort** for import sorting\n- **ruff** for linting\n\n## Reference\n\nSee skill: `python-patterns` for comprehensive Python idioms and patterns.\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.py&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/*.pyi&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>Python Coding Style<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/coding-style.md\">common/coding-style.md<\/a> with Python specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>Standards<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Follow <strong>PEP 8<\/strong> conventions<\/li>\n<li>Use <strong>type annotations<\/strong> on all function signatures<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Immutability<\/h2>\n<p>Prefer immutable data structures:<\/p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-python\">from dataclasses import dataclass\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass User:\n    name: str\n    email: str\n\nfrom typing import NamedTuple\n\nclass Point(NamedTuple):\n    x: float\n    y: float\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Formatting<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>black<\/strong> for code formatting<\/li>\n<li><strong>isort<\/strong> for import sorting<\/li>\n<li><strong>ruff<\/strong> for linting<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Reference<\/h2>\n<p>See skill: <code>python-patterns<\/code> for comprehensive Python idioms and patterns.<\/p>\n"
    },

      "type": "rule",

      "metadata": {},

      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.py\"\n  - \"**/*.pyi\"\n---\n> This file extends common/hooks.md with Python specific content.\nConfigure in :\n**black/ruff**: Auto-format  files after edit\n**mypy/pyright**: Run type checking after editing  files\nWarn about  statements in edited files (use  module instead)",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.py\"\n  - \"**/*.pyi\"\n---\n# Python Hooks\n\n> This file extends [common/hooks.md](../common/hooks.md) with Python specific content.\n\n## PostToolUse Hooks\n\nConfigure in `~/.claude/settings.json`:\n\n- **black/ruff**: Auto-format `.py` files after edit\n- **mypy/pyright**: Run type checking after editing `.py` files\n\n## Warnings\n\n- Warn about `print()` statements in edited files (use `logging` module instead)\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.py&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/*.pyi&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>Python Hooks<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/hooks.md\">common/hooks.md<\/a> with Python specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>PostToolUse Hooks<\/h2>\n<p>Configure in <code>~/.claude/settings.json<\/code>:<\/p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>black/ruff<\/strong>: Auto-format <code>.py<\/code> files after edit<\/li>\n<li><strong>mypy/pyright<\/strong>: Run type checking after editing <code>.py<\/code> files<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Warnings<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Warn about <code>print()<\/code> statements in edited files (use <code>logging<\/code> module instead)<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n"
    },

      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.py\"\n  - \"**/*.pyi\"\n---\n> This file extends common/patterns.md with Python specific content.\nUse context managers ( statement) for resource management\nUse generators for lazy evaluation and memory-efficient iteration\nSee skill:  for comprehensive patterns including decorators, co",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.py\"\n  - \"**/*.pyi\"\n---\n# Python Patterns\n\n> This file extends [common/patterns.md](../common/patterns.md) with Python specific content.\n\n## Protocol (Duck Typing)\n\n```python\nfrom typing import Protocol\n\nclass Repository(Protocol):\n    def find_by_id(self, id: str) -> dict | None: ...\n    def save(self, entity: dict) -> dict: ...\n```\n\n## Dataclasses as DTOs\n\n```python\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\n@dataclass\nclass CreateUserRequest:\n    name: str\n    email: str\n    age: int | None = None\n```\n\n## Context Managers & Generators\n\n- Use context managers (`with` statement) for resource management\n- Use generators for lazy evaluation and memory-efficient iteration\n\n## Reference\n\nSee skill: `python-patterns` for comprehensive patterns including decorators, concurrency, and package organization.\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.py&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/*.pyi&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>Python Patterns<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/patterns.md\">common/patterns.md<\/a> with Python specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>Protocol (Duck Typing)<\/h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-python\">from typing import Protocol\n\nclass Repository(Protocol):\n    def find_by_id(self, id: str) -&gt; dict | None: ...\n    def save(self, entity: dict) -&gt; dict: ...\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Dataclasses as DTOs<\/h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-python\">from dataclasses import dataclass\n\n@dataclass\nclass CreateUserRequest:\n    name: str\n    email: str\n    age: int | None = None\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Context Managers &amp; Generators<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Use context managers (<code>with<\/code> statement) for resource management<\/li>\n<li>Use generators for lazy evaluation and memory-efficient iteration<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Reference<\/h2>\n<p>See skill: <code>python-patterns<\/code> for comprehensive patterns including decorators, concurrency, and package organization.<\/p>\n"
    },

      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.py\"\n  - \"**/*.pyi\"\n---\n> This file extends common/security.md with Python specific content.\nUse **bandit** for static security analysis:\n  \nSee skill:  for Django-specific security guidelines (if applicable).",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.py\"\n  - \"**/*.pyi\"\n---\n# Python Security\n\n> This file extends [common/security.md](../common/security.md) with Python specific content.\n\n## Secret Management\n\n```python\nimport os\nfrom dotenv import load_dotenv\n\nload_dotenv()\n\napi_key = os.environ[\"OPENAI_API_KEY\"]  # Raises KeyError if missing\n```\n\n## Security Scanning\n\n- Use **bandit** for static security analysis:\n  ```bash\n  bandit -r src/\n  ```\n\n## Reference\n\nSee skill: `django-security` for Django-specific security guidelines (if applicable).\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.py&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/*.pyi&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>Python Security<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/security.md\">common/security.md<\/a> with Python specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>Secret Management<\/h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-python\">import os\nfrom dotenv import load_dotenv\n\nload_dotenv()\n\napi_key = os.environ[&quot;OPENAI_API_KEY&quot;]  # Raises KeyError if missing\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Security Scanning<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Use <strong>bandit<\/strong> for static security analysis:<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">bandit -r src/\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Reference<\/h2>\n<p>See skill: <code>django-security<\/code> for Django-specific security guidelines (if applicable).<\/p>\n"

      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.py\"\n  - \"**/*.pyi\"\n---\n> This file extends common/testing.md with Python specific content.\nUse **pytest** as the testing framework.\nUse  for test categorization:\nSee skill:  for detailed pytest patterns and fixtures.",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.py\"\n  - \"**/*.pyi\"\n---\n# Python Testing\n\n> This file extends [common/testing.md](../common/testing.md) with Python specific content.\n\n## Framework\n\nUse **pytest** as the testing framework.\n\n## Coverage\n\n```bash\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing\n```\n\n## Test Organization\n\nUse `pytest.mark` for test categorization:\n\n```python\nimport pytest\n\n@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_calculate_total():\n    ...\n\n@pytest.mark.integration\ndef test_database_connection():\n    ...\n```\n\n## Reference\n\nSee skill: `python-testing` for detailed pytest patterns and fixtures.\n",

    {
      "type": "rule",
      "subtype": "rule_md",
      "path": "rules/rust/coding-style.md",
      "title": "Rust Coding Style",
      "description": "--- paths:   - \"**/*.rs\" --- > This file extends common/coding-style.md with Rust-specific content. **rustfmt** for enfo",
      "metadata": {},
      "risks": [],
      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.rs\"\n---\n> This file extends common/coding-style.md with Rust-specific content.\n**rustfmt** for enforcement — always run  before committing\n**clippy** for lints —  (treat warnings as errors)\n4-space indent (rustfmt default)\nMax line width: 100 characters (rustfmt default)\nRust va",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.rs\"\n---\n# Rust Coding Style\n\n> This file extends [common/coding-style.md](../common/coding-style.md) with Rust-specific content.\n\n## Formatting\n\n- **rustfmt** for enforcement — always run `cargo fmt` before committing\n- **clippy** for lints — `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` (treat warnings as errors)\n- 4-space indent (rustfmt default)\n- Max line width: 100 characters (rustfmt default)\n\n## Immutability\n\nRust variables are immutable by default — embrace this:\n\n- Use `let` by default; only use `let mut` when mutation is required\n- Prefer returning new values over mutating in place\n- Use `Cow<'_, T>` when a function may or may not need to allocate\n\n```rust\nuse std::borrow::Cow;\n\n// GOOD — immutable by default, new value returned\nfn normalize(input: &str) -> Cow<'_, str> {\n    if input.contains(' ') {\n        Cow::Owned(input.replace(' ', \"_\"))\n    } else {\n        Cow::Borrowed(input)\n    }\n}\n\n// BAD — unnecessary mutation\nfn normalize_bad(input: &mut String) {\n    *input = input.replace(' ', \"_\");\n}\n```\n\n## Naming\n\nFollow standard Rust conventions:\n- `snake_case` for functions, methods, variables, modules, crates\n- `PascalCase` (UpperCamelCase) for types, traits, enums, type parameters\n- `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` for constants and statics\n- Lifetimes: short lowercase (`'a`, `'de`) — descriptive names for complex cases (`'input`)\n\n## Ownership and Borrowing\n\n- Borrow (`&T`) by default; take ownership only when you need to store or consume\n- Never clone to satisfy the borrow checker without understanding the root cause\n- Accept `&str` over `String`, `&[T]` over `Vec<T>` in function parameters\n- Use `impl Into<String>` for constructors that need to own a `String`\n\n```rust\n// GOOD — borrows when ownership isn't needed\nfn word_count(text: &str) -> usize {\n    text.split_whitespace().count()\n}\n\n// GOOD — takes ownership in constructor via Into\nfn new(name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n    Self { name: name.into() }\n}\n\n// BAD — takes String when &str suffices\nfn word_count_bad(text: String) -> usize {\n    text.split_whitespace().count()\n}\n```\n\n## Error Handling\n\n- Use `Result<T, E>` and `?` for propagation — never `unwrap()` in production code\n- **Libraries**: define typed errors with `thiserror`\n- **Applications**: use `anyhow` for flexible error context\n- Add context with `.with_context(|| format!(\"failed to ...\"))?`\n- Reserve `unwrap()` / `expect()` for tests and truly unreachable states\n\n```rust\n// GOOD — library error with thiserror\n#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]\npub enum ConfigError {\n    #[error(\"failed to read config: {0}\")]\n    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),\n    #[error(\"invalid config format: {0}\")]\n    Parse(String),\n}\n\n// GOOD — application error with anyhow\nuse anyhow::Context;\n\nfn load_config(path: &str) -> anyhow::Result<Config> {\n    let content = std::fs::read_to_string(path)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read {path}\"))?;\n    toml::from_str(&content)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to parse {path}\"))\n}\n```\n\n## Iterators Over Loops\n\nPrefer iterator chains for transformations; use loops for complex control flow:\n\n```rust\n// GOOD — declarative and composable\nlet active_emails: Vec<&str> = users.iter()\n    .filter(|u| u.is_active)\n    .map(|u| u.email.as_str())\n    .collect();\n\n// GOOD — loop for complex logic with early returns\nfor user in &users {\n    if let Some(verified) = verify_email(&user.email)? {\n        send_welcome(&verified)?;\n    }\n}\n```\n\n## Module Organization\n\nOrganize by domain, not by type:\n\n```text\nsrc/\n├── main.rs\n├── lib.rs\n├── auth/           # Domain module\n│   ├── mod.rs\n│   ├── token.rs\n│   └── middleware.rs\n├── orders/         # Domain module\n│   ├── mod.rs\n│   ├── model.rs\n│   └── service.rs\n└── db/             # Infrastructure\n    ├── mod.rs\n    └── pool.rs\n```\n\n## Visibility\n\n- Default to private; use `pub(crate)` for internal sharing\n- Only mark `pub` what is part of the crate's public API\n- Re-export public API from `lib.rs`\n\n## References\n\nSee skill: `rust-patterns` for comprehensive Rust idioms and patterns.\n",

      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.rs\"\n  - \"**/Cargo.toml\"\n---\n# Rust Hooks\n\n> This file extends [common/hooks.md](../common/hooks.md) with Rust-specific content.\n\n## PostToolUse Hooks\n\nConfigure in `~/.claude/settings.json`:\n\n- **cargo fmt**: Auto-format `.rs` files after edit\n- **cargo clippy**: Run lint checks after editing Rust files\n- **cargo check**: Verify compilation after changes (faster than `cargo build`)\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.rs&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/Cargo.toml&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>Rust Hooks<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/hooks.md\">common/hooks.md<\/a> with Rust-specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>PostToolUse Hooks<\/h2>\n<p>Configure in <code>~/.claude/settings.json<\/code>:<\/p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>cargo fmt<\/strong>: Auto-format <code>.rs<\/code> files after edit<\/li>\n<li><strong>cargo clippy<\/strong>: Run lint checks after editing Rust files<\/li>\n<li><strong>cargo check<\/strong>: Verify compilation after changes (faster than <code>cargo build<\/code>)<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n"

      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.rs\"\n---\n> This file extends common/patterns.md with Rust-specific content.\nEncapsulate data access behind a trait:\nConcrete implementations handle storage details (Postgres, SQLite, in-memory for tests).\nBusiness logic in service structs; inject dependencies via constructor:\nPre",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.rs\"\n---\n# Rust Patterns\n\n> This file extends [common/patterns.md](../common/patterns.md) with Rust-specific content.\n\n## Repository Pattern with Traits\n\nEncapsulate data access behind a trait:\n\n```rust\npub trait OrderRepository: Send + Sync {\n    fn find_by_id(&self, id: u64) -> Result<Option<Order>, StorageError>;\n    fn find_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<Order>, StorageError>;\n    fn save(&self, order: &Order) -> Result<Order, StorageError>;\n    fn delete(&self, id: u64) -> Result<(), StorageError>;\n}\n```\n\nConcrete implementations handle storage details (Postgres, SQLite, in-memory for tests).\n\n## Service Layer\n\nBusiness logic in service structs; inject dependencies via constructor:\n\n```rust\npub struct OrderService {\n    repo: Box<dyn OrderRepository>,\n    payment: Box<dyn PaymentGateway>,\n}\n\nimpl OrderService {\n    pub fn new(repo: Box<dyn OrderRepository>, payment: Box<dyn PaymentGateway>) -> Self {\n        Self { repo, payment }\n    }\n\n    pub fn place_order(&self, request: CreateOrderRequest) -> anyhow::Result<OrderSummary> {\n        let order = Order::from(request);\n        self.payment.charge(order.total())?;\n        let saved = self.repo.save(&order)?;\n        Ok(OrderSummary::from(saved))\n    }\n}\n```\n\n## Newtype Pattern for Type Safety\n\nPrevent argument mix-ups with distinct wrapper types:\n\n```rust\nstruct UserId(u64);\nstruct OrderId(u64);\n\nfn get_order(user: UserId, order: OrderId) -> anyhow::Result<Order> {\n    // Can't accidentally swap user and order IDs at call sites\n    todo!()\n}\n```\n\n## Enum State Machines\n\nModel states as enums — make illegal states unrepresentable:\n\n```rust\nenum ConnectionState {\n    Disconnected,\n    Connecting { attempt: u32 },\n    Connected { session_id: String },\n    Failed { reason: String, retries: u32 },\n}\n\nfn handle(state: &ConnectionState) {\n    match state {\n        ConnectionState::Disconnected => connect(),\n        ConnectionState::Connecting { attempt } if *attempt > 3 => abort(),\n        ConnectionState::Connecting { .. } => wait(),\n        ConnectionState::Connected { session_id } => use_session(session_id),\n        ConnectionState::Failed { retries, .. } if *retries < 5 => retry(),\n        ConnectionState::Failed { reason, .. } => log_failure(reason),\n    }\n}\n```\n\nAlways match exhaustively — no wildcard `_` for business-critical enums.\n\n## Builder Pattern\n\nUse for structs with many optional parameters:\n\n```rust\npub struct ServerConfig {\n    host: String,\n    port: u16,\n    max_connections: usize,\n}\n\nimpl ServerConfig {\n    pub fn builder(host: impl Into<String>, port: u16) -> ServerConfigBuilder {\n        ServerConfigBuilder {\n            host: host.into(),\n            port,\n            max_connections: 100,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\npub struct ServerConfigBuilder {\n    host: String,\n    port: u16,\n    max_connections: usize,\n}\n\nimpl ServerConfigBuilder {\n    pub fn max_connections(mut self, n: usize) -> Self {\n        self.max_connections = n;\n        self\n    }\n\n    pub fn build(self) -> ServerConfig {\n        ServerConfig {\n            host: self.host,\n            port: self.port,\n            max_connections: self.max_connections,\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n\n## Sealed Traits for Extensibility Control\n\nUse a private module to seal a trait, preventing external implementations:\n\n```rust\nmod private {\n    pub trait Sealed {}\n}\n\npub trait Format: private::Sealed {\n    fn encode(&self, data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>;\n}\n\npub struct Json;\nimpl private::Sealed for Json {}\nimpl Format for Json {\n    fn encode(&self, data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> { todo!() }\n}\n```\n\n## API Response Envelope\n\nConsistent API responses using a generic enum:\n\n```rust\n#[derive(Debug, serde::Serialize)]\n#[serde(tag = \"status\")]\npub enum ApiResponse<T: serde::Serialize> {\n    #[serde(rename = \"ok\")]\n    Ok { data: T },\n    #[serde(rename = \"error\")]\n    Error { message: String },\n}\n```\n\n## References\n\nSee skill: `rust-patterns` for comprehensive patterns including ownership, traits, generics, concurrency, and async.\n",

connect(),\n        ConnectionState::Connecting { attempt } if *attempt &gt; 3 =&gt; abort(),\n        ConnectionState::Connecting { .. } =&gt; wait(),\n        ConnectionState::Connected { session_id } =&gt; ServerConfigBuilder {\n        ServerConfigBuilder {\n            host: host.into(),\n            port,\n            max_connections: 100,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\npub struct ServerConfigBuilder {\n    host: String,\n    port: u16,\n    max_connections: usize,\n}\n\nimpl ServerConfigBuilder {\n    pub fn max_connections(mut self, n: usize) -&gt; Self {\n        self.max_connections = n;\n        self\n    }\n\n    pub fn build(self) -&gt; ServerConfig {\n        ServerConfig {\n            host: self.host,\n            port: self.port,\n            max_connections: self.max_connections,\n        }\n    }\n}\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Sealed Traits for Extensibility Control<\/h2>\n<p>Use a private module to seal a trait, preventing external implementations:<\/p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">mod private {\n    pub trait Sealed {}\n}\n\npub trait Format: private::Sealed {\n    fn encode(&amp;self, data: &amp;[u8]) -&gt; Vec&lt;u8&gt;;\n}\n\npub struct Json;\nimpl private::Sealed for Json {}\nimpl Format for Json {\n    fn encode(&amp;self, data: &amp;[u8]) -&gt; Vec&lt;u8&gt; { todo!() }\n}\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>API Response Envelope<\/h2>\n<p>Consistent API responses using a generic enum:<\/p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">#[derive(Debug, serde::Serialize)]\n#[serde(tag = &quot;status&quot;)]\npub enum ApiResponse&lt;T: serde::Serialize&gt; {\n    #[serde(rename = &quot;ok&quot;)]\n    Ok { data: T },\n    #[serde(rename = &quot;error&quot;)]\n    Error { message: String },\n}\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>References<\/h2>\n<p>See skill: <code>rust-patterns<\/code> for comprehensive patterns including ownership, traits, generics, concurrency, and async.<\/p>\n"

      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.rs\"\n---\n> This file extends common/security.md with Rust-specific content.\nNever hardcode API keys, tokens, or credentials in source code\nUse environment variables: \nFail fast if required secrets are missing at startup\nKeep  files in \nAlways use parameterized queries — never for",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.rs\"\n---\n# Rust Security\n\n> This file extends [common/security.md](../common/security.md) with Rust-specific content.\n\n## Secrets Management\n\n- Never hardcode API keys, tokens, or credentials in source code\n- Use environment variables: `std::env::var(\"API_KEY\")`\n- Fail fast if required secrets are missing at startup\n- Keep `.env` files in `.gitignore`\n\n```rust\n// BAD\nconst API_KEY: &str = \"sk-abc123...\";\n\n// GOOD — environment variable with early validation\nfn load_api_key() -> anyhow::Result<String> {\n    std::env::var(\"PAYMENT_API_KEY\")\n        .context(\"PAYMENT_API_KEY must be set\")\n}\n```\n\n## SQL Injection Prevention\n\n- Always use parameterized queries — never format user input into SQL strings\n- Use query builder or ORM (sqlx, diesel, sea-orm) with bind parameters\n\n```rust\n// BAD — SQL injection via format string\nlet query = format!(\"SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '{name}'\");\nsqlx::query(&query).fetch_one(&pool).await?;\n\n// GOOD — parameterized query with sqlx\n// Placeholder syntax varies by backend: Postgres: $1  |  MySQL: ?  |  SQLite: $1\nsqlx::query(\"SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = $1\")\n    .bind(&name)\n    .fetch_one(&pool)\n    .await?;\n```\n\n## Input Validation\n\n- Validate all user input at system boundaries before processing\n- Use the type system to enforce invariants (newtype pattern)\n- Parse, don't validate — convert unstructured data to typed structs at the boundary\n- Reject invalid input with clear error messages\n\n```rust\n// Parse, don't validate — invalid states are unrepresentable\npub struct Email(String);\n\nimpl Email {\n    pub fn parse(input: &str) -> Result<Self, ValidationError> {\n        let trimmed = input.trim();\n        let at_pos = trimmed.find('@')\n            .filter(|&p| p > 0 && p < trimmed.len() - 1)\n            .ok_or_else(|| ValidationError::InvalidEmail(input.to_string()))?;\n        let domain = &trimmed[at_pos + 1..];\n        if trimmed.len() > 254 || !domain.contains('.') {\n            return Err(ValidationError::InvalidEmail(input.to_string()));\n        }\n        // For production use, prefer a validated email crate (e.g., `email_address`)\n        Ok(Self(trimmed.to_string()))\n    }\n\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.0\n    }\n}\n```\n\n## Unsafe Code\n\n- Minimize `unsafe` blocks — prefer safe abstractions\n- Every `unsafe` block must have a `// SAFETY:` FFI wrappers around C libraries\n\n```rust\n// GOOD — safety comment documents ALL required invariants\nlet widget: &Widget = {\n    // SAFETY: `ptr` is non-null, aligned, points to an initialized `cargo audit` to scan for known CVEs in dependencies\n- Run `cargo deny check` for license and advisory compliance\n- Use `cargo tree` to audit transitive dependencies\n- Keep dependencies updated — set up Dependabot or Renovate\n- Minimize dependency count — evaluate before adding new crates\n\n```bash\n# Security audit\ncargo audit\n\n# Deny advisories, duplicate versions, and restricted in API responses\n- Log detailed errors server-side; return generic messages to clients\n- Use `tracing` or `log` for structured server-side logging\n\n```rust\n// Map errors to appropriate status tracing::error!(order_id = id, error = %e, \"unexpected error\");\n        Err((StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, \"Internal server error\"))\n    }\n}\n```\n\n## References\n\nSee skill: `rust-patterns` for unsafe code guidelines and ownership patterns.\nSee skill: `security-review` for general security checklists.\n",

      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.rs\"\n---\n> This file extends common/testing.md with Rust-specific content.\n**** with  modules for unit tests\n**rstest** for parameterized tests and fixtures\n**proptest** for property-based testing\n**mockall** for trait-based mocking\n**** for async tests\nUnit tests go inside  modu",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.rs\"\n---\n# Rust Testing\n\n> This file extends [common/testing.md](../common/testing.md) with Rust-specific content.\n\n## Test Framework\n\n- **`#[test]`** with `#[cfg(test)]` modules for unit tests\n- **rstest** for parameterized tests and fixtures\n- **proptest** for property-based testing\n- **mockall** for trait-based mocking\n- **`#[tokio::test]`** for async tests\n\n## Test Organization\n\n```text\nmy_crate/\n├── src/\n│   ├── lib.rs           # Unit tests in #[cfg(test)] modules\n│   ├── auth/\n│   │   └── mod.rs       # #[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }\n│   └── orders/\n│       └── service.rs   # #[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }\n├── tests/               # Integration tests (each file = separate binary)\n│   ├── api_test.rs\n│   ├── db_test.rs\n│   └── common/          # Shared test utilities\n│       └── mod.rs\n└── benches/             # Criterion benchmarks\n    └── benchmark.rs\n```\n\nUnit tests go inside `#[cfg(test)]` modules in the same file. Integration tests go in `tests/`.\n\n## Unit Test Pattern\n\n```rust\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn creates_user_with_valid_email() {\n        let user = User::new(\"Alice\", \"alice@example.com\").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(user.name, \"Alice\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rejects_invalid_email() {\n        let result = User::new(\"Bob\", \"not-an-email\");\n        assert!(result.is_err());\n        assert!(result.unwrap_err().to_string().contains(\"invalid email\"));\n    }\n}\n```\n\n## Parameterized Tests\n\n```rust\nuse rstest::rstest;\n\n#[rstest]\n#[case(\"hello\", 5)]\n#[case(\"\", 0)]\n#[case(\"rust\", 4)]\nfn test_string_length(#[case] input: &str, #[case] expected: usize) {\n    assert_eq!(input.len(), expected);\n}\n```\n\n## Async Tests\n\n```rust\n#[tokio::test]\nasync fn fetches_data_successfully() {\n    let client = TestClient::new().await;\n    let result = client.get(\"/data\").await;\n    assert!(result.is_ok());\n}\n```\n\n## Mocking with mockall\n\nDefine traits in production code; generate mocks in test modules:\n\n```rust\n// Production trait — pub so integration tests can import it\npub trait UserRepository {\n    fn find_by_id(&self, id: u64) -> Option<User>;\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use mockall::predicate::eq;\n\n    mockall::mock! {\n        pub Repo {}\n        impl UserRepository for Repo {\n            fn find_by_id(&self, id: u64) -> Option<User>;\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn service_returns_user_when_found() {\n        let mut mock = MockRepo::new();\n        mock.expect_find_by_id()\n            .with(eq(42))\n            .times(1)\n            .returning(|_| Some(User { id: 42, name: \"Alice\".into() }));\n\n        let service = UserService::new(Box::new(mock));\n        let user = service.get_user(42).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(user.name, \"Alice\");\n    }\n}\n```\n\n## Test Naming\n\nUse descriptive names that explain the scenario:\n- `creates_user_with_valid_email()`\n- `rejects_order_when_insufficient_stock()`\n- `returns_none_when_not_found()`\n\n## Coverage\n\n- Target 80%+ line coverage\n- Use **cargo-llvm-cov** for coverage reporting\n- Focus on business logic — exclude generated code and FFI bindings\n\n```bash\ncargo llvm-cov                       # Summary\ncargo llvm-cov --html                # HTML report\ncargo llvm-cov --fail-under-lines 80 # Fail if below threshold\n```\n\n## Testing Commands\n\n```bash\ncargo test                       # Run all tests\ncargo test -- --nocapture        # Show println output\ncargo test test_name             # Run tests matching pattern\ncargo test --lib                 # Unit tests only\ncargo test --test api_test       # Specific integration test (tests/api_test.rs)\ncargo test --doc                 # Doc tests only\n```\n\n## References\n\nSee skill: `rust-testing` for comprehensive testing patterns including property-based testing, fixtures, and benchmarking with Criterion.\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;**/*.rs&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>Rust Testing<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/testing.md\">common/testing.md<\/a> with Rust-specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>Test Framework<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong><code>#[test]<\/code><\/strong> with <code>#[cfg(test)]<\/code> modules for unit tests<\/li>\n<li><strong>rstest<\/strong> for parameterized tests and fixtures<\/li>\n<li><strong>proptest<\/strong> for property-based testing<\/li>\n<li><strong>mockall<\/strong> for trait-based mocking<\/li>\n<li><strong><code>#[tokio::test]<\/code><\/strong> for async tests<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Test Organization<\/h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-text\">my_crate/\n├── src/\n│   ├── lib.rs           # Unit tests in #[cfg(test)] modules\n│   ├── auth/\n│   │   └── mod.rs       # #[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }\n│   └── orders/\n│       └── service.rs   # #[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }\n├── tests/               # Integration tests (each file = separate binary)\n│   ├── api_test.rs\n│   ├── db_test.rs\n│   └── common/          # Shared test utilities\n│       └── mod.rs\n└── benches/             # Criterion benchmarks\n    └── benchmark.rs\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<p>Unit tests go inside <code>#[cfg(test)]<\/code> modules in the same file. Integration tests go in <code>tests/<\/code>.<\/p>\n<h2>Unit Test Pattern<\/h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn creates_user_with_valid_email() {\n        let user = User::new(&quot;Alice&quot;, &quot;alice@example.com&quot;).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(user.name, &quot;Alice&quot;);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rejects_invalid_email() {\n        let result = User::new(&quot;Bob&quot;, &quot;not-an-email&quot;);\n        assert!(result.is_err());\n        assert!(result.unwrap_err().to_string().contains(&quot;invalid email&quot;));\n    }\n}\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Parameterized Tests<\/h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">use rstest::rstest;\n\n#[rstest]\n#[case(&quot;hello&quot;, 5)]\n#[case(&quot;&quot;, 0)]\n#[case(&quot;rust&quot;, 4)]\nfn test_string_length(#[case] input: &amp;str, #[case] expected: usize) {\n    assert_eq!(input.len(), expected);\n}\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Async Tests<\/h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">#[tokio::test]\nasync fn fetches_data_successfully() {\n    let client = TestClient::new().await;\n    let result = client.get(&quot;/data&quot;).await;\n    assert!(result.is_ok());\n}\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Mocking with mockall<\/h2>\n<p>Define traits in production code; generate mocks in test modules:<\/p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-rust\">// Production trait — pub so integration tests can import it\npub trait UserRepository {\n    fn find_by_id(&amp;self, id: u64) -&gt; Option&lt;User&gt;;\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use mockall::predicate::eq;\n\n    mockall::mock! {\n        pub Repo {}\n        impl UserRepository for Repo {\n            fn find_by_id(&amp;self, id: u64) -&gt; Option&lt;User&gt;;\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn service_returns_user_when_found() {\n        let mut mock = MockRepo::new();\n        mock.expect_find_by_id()\n            .with(eq(42))\n            .times(1)\n            .returning(|_| Some(User { id: 42, name: &quot;Alice&quot;.into() }));\n\n        let service = UserService::new(Box::new(mock));\n        let user = service.get_user(42).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(user.name, &quot;Alice&quot;);\n    }\n}\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Test Naming<\/h2>\n<p>Use descriptive names that explain the scenario:<\/p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>creates_user_with_valid_email()<\/code><\/li>\n<li><code>rejects_order_when_insufficient_stock()<\/code><\/li>\n<li><code>returns_none_when_not_found()<\/code><\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Coverage<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Target 80%+ line coverage<\/li>\n<li>Use <strong>cargo-llvm-cov<\/strong> for coverage reporting<\/li>\n<li>Focus on business logic — exclude generated code and FFI bindings<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">cargo llvm-cov                       # Summary\ncargo llvm-cov --html                # HTML report\ncargo llvm-cov --fail-under-lines 80 # Fail if below threshold\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Testing Commands<\/h2>\n<pre><code class=\"language-bash\">cargo test                       # Run all tests\ncargo test -- --nocapture        # Show println output\ncargo test test_name             # Run tests matching pattern\ncargo test --lib                 # Unit tests only\ncargo test --test api_test       # Specific integration test (tests/api_test.rs)\ncargo test --doc                 # Doc tests only\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>References<\/h2>\n<p>See skill: <code>rust-testing<\/code> for comprehensive testing patterns including property-based testing, fixtures, and benchmarking with Criterion.<\/p>\n"

      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.swift\"\n  - \"**/Package.swift\"\n---\n> This file extends common/coding-style.md with Swift specific content.\n**SwiftFormat** for auto-formatting, **SwiftLint** for style enforcement\nis bundled with Xcode 16+ as an alternative\nPrefer  over  — define everything as  and only change to",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.swift\"\n  - \"**/Package.swift\"\n---\n# Swift Coding Style\n\n> This file extends [common/coding-style.md](../common/coding-style.md) with Swift specific content.\n\n## Formatting\n\n- **SwiftFormat** for auto-formatting, **SwiftLint** for style enforcement\n- `swift-format` is bundled with Xcode 16+ as an alternative\n\n## Immutability\n\n- Prefer `let` over `var` — define everything as `let` and only change to `var` if the compiler requires it\n- Use `struct` with value semantics by default; use `class` only when identity or reference semantics are needed\n\n## Naming\n\nFollow [Apple API Design Guidelines](https://www.swift.org/documentation/api-design-guidelines/):\n\n- Clarity at the point of use — omit needless words\n- Name methods and properties for their roles, not their types\n- Use `static let` for constants over global constants\n\n## Error Handling\n\nUse typed throws (Swift 6+) and pattern matching:\n\n```swift\nfunc load(id: String) throws(LoadError) -> Item {\n    guard let data = try? read(from: path) else {\n        throw .fileNotFound(id)\n    }\n    return try decode(data)\n}\n```\n\n## Concurrency\n\nEnable Swift 6 strict concurrency checking. Prefer:\n\n- `Sendable` value types for data crossing isolation boundaries\n- Actors for shared mutable state\n- Structured concurrency (`async let`, `TaskGroup`) over unstructured `Task {}`\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.swift&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/Package.swift&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>Swift Coding Style<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/coding-style.md\">common/coding-style.md<\/a> with Swift specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>Formatting<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>SwiftFormat<\/strong> for auto-formatting, <strong>SwiftLint<\/strong> for style enforcement<\/li>\n<li><code>swift-format<\/code> is bundled with Xcode 16+ as an alternative<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Immutability<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Prefer <code>let<\/code> over <code>var<\/code> — define everything as <code>let<\/code> and only change to <code>var<\/code> if the compiler requires it<\/li>\n<li>Use <code>struct<\/code> with value semantics by default; use <code>class<\/code> only when identity or reference semantics are needed<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Naming<\/h2>\n<p>Follow <a href=\"https://www.swift.org/documentation/api-design-guidelines/\">Apple API Design Guidelines<\/a>:<\/p>\n<ul>\n<li>Clarity at the point of use — omit needless words<\/li>\n<li>Name methods and properties for their roles, not their types<\/li>\n<li>Use <code>static let<\/code> for constants over global constants<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Error Handling<\/h2>\n<p>Use typed throws (Swift 6+) and pattern matching:<\/p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-swift\">func load(id: String) throws(LoadError) -&gt; Item {\n    guard let data = try? read(from: path) else {\n        throw .fileNotFound(id)\n    }\n    return try decode(data)\n}\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Concurrency<\/h2>\n<p>Enable Swift 6 strict concurrency checking. Prefer:<\/p>\n<ul>\n<li><code>Sendable<\/code> value types for data crossing isolation boundaries<\/li>\n<li>Actors for shared mutable state<\/li>\n<li>Structured concurrency (<code>async let<\/code>, <code>TaskGroup<\/code>) over unstructured <code>Task {}<\/code><\/li>\n<\/ul>\n"

      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.swift\"\n  - \"**/Package.swift\"\n---\n> This file extends common/hooks.md with Swift specific content.\nConfigure in :\n**SwiftFormat**: Auto-format  files after edit\n**SwiftLint**: Run lint checks after editing  files\n**swift build**: Type-check modified packages after edit\nFlag  sta",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.swift\"\n  - \"**/Package.swift\"\n---\n# Swift Hooks\n\n> This file extends [common/hooks.md](../common/hooks.md) with Swift specific content.\n\n## PostToolUse Hooks\n\nConfigure in `~/.claude/settings.json`:\n\n- **SwiftFormat**: Auto-format `.swift` files after edit\n- **SwiftLint**: Run lint checks after editing `.swift` files\n- **swift build**: Type-check modified packages after edit\n\n## Warning\n\nFlag `print()` statements — use `os.Logger` or structured logging instead for production code.\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.swift&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/Package.swift&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>Swift Hooks<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/hooks.md\">common/hooks.md<\/a> with Swift specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>PostToolUse Hooks<\/h2>\n<p>Configure in <code>~/.claude/settings.json<\/code>:<\/p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>SwiftFormat<\/strong>: Auto-format <code>.swift<\/code> files after edit<\/li>\n<li><strong>SwiftLint<\/strong>: Run lint checks after editing <code>.swift<\/code> files<\/li>\n<li><strong>swift build<\/strong>: Type-check modified packages after edit<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Warning<\/h2>\n<p>Flag <code>print()<\/code> statements — use <code>os.Logger<\/code> or structured logging instead for production code.<\/p>\n"

      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.swift\"\n  - \"**/Package.swift\"\n---\n> This file extends common/patterns.md with Swift specific content.\nDefine small, focused protocols. Use protocol extensions for shared defaults:\nUse structs for data transfer objects and models\nUse enums with associated values to model distinct",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.swift\"\n  - \"**/Package.swift\"\n---\n# Swift Patterns\n\n> This file extends [common/patterns.md](../common/patterns.md) with Swift specific content.\n\n## Protocol-Oriented Design\n\nDefine small, focused protocols. Use protocol extensions for shared defaults:\n\n```swift\nprotocol Repository: Sendable {\n    associatedtype Item: Identifiable & Sendable\n    func find(by id: Item.ID) async throws -> Item?\n    func save(_ item: Item) async throws\n}\n```\n\n## Value Types\n\n- Use structs for data transfer objects and models\n- Use enums with associated values to model distinct states:\n\n```swift\nenum LoadState<T: Sendable>: Sendable {\n    case idle\n    case loading\n    case loaded(T)\n    case failed(Error)\n}\n```\n\n## Actor Pattern\n\nUse actors for shared mutable state instead of locks or dispatch queues:\n\n```swift\nactor Cache<Key: Hashable & Sendable, Value: Sendable> {\n    private var storage: [Key: Value] = [:]\n\n    func get(_ key: Key) -> Value? { storage[key] }\n    func set(_ key: Key, value: Value) { storage[key] = value }\n}\n```\n\n## Dependency Injection\n\nInject protocols with default parameters — production uses defaults, tests inject mocks:\n\n```swift\nstruct UserService {\n    private let repository: any UserRepository\n\n    init(repository: any UserRepository = DefaultUserRepository()) {\n        self.repository = repository\n    }\n}\n```\n\n## References\n\nSee skill: `swift-actor-persistence` for actor-based persistence patterns.\nSee skill: `swift-protocol-di-testing` for protocol-based DI and testing.\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.swift&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/Package.swift&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>Swift Patterns<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/patterns.md\">common/patterns.md<\/a> with Swift specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>Protocol-Oriented Design<\/h2>\n<p>Define small, focused protocols. Use protocol extensions for shared defaults:<\/p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-swift\">protocol Repository: Sendable {\n    associatedtype Item: Identifiable &amp; Sendable\n    func find(by id: Item.ID) async throws -&gt; Item?\n    func save(_ item: Item) async throws\n}\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Value Types<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Use structs for data transfer objects and models<\/li>\n<li>Use enums with associated values to model distinct states:<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<pre><code class=\"language-swift\">enum LoadState&lt;T: Sendable&gt;: Sendable {\n    case idle\n    case loading\n    case loaded(T)\n    case failed(Error)\n}\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Actor Pattern<\/h2>\n<p>Use actors for shared mutable state instead of locks or dispatch queues:<\/p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-swift\">actor Cache&lt;Key: Hashable &amp; Sendable, Value: Sendable&gt; {\n    private var storage: [Key: Value] = [:]\n\n    func get(_ key: Key) -&gt; Value? { storage[key] }\n    func set(_ key: Key, value: Value) { storage[key] = value }\n}\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Dependency Injection<\/h2>\n<p>Inject protocols with default parameters — production uses defaults, tests inject mocks:<\/p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-swift\">struct UserService {\n    private let repository: any UserRepository\n\n    init(repository: any UserRepository = DefaultUserRepository()) {\n        self.repository = repository\n    }\n}\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>References<\/h2>\n<p>See skill: <code>swift-actor-persistence<\/code> for actor-based persistence patterns.\nSee skill: <code>swift-protocol-di-testing<\/code> for protocol-based DI and testing.<\/p>\n"
    },

      "contentPreview": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.swift\"\n  - \"**/Package.swift\"\n---\n> This file extends common/security.md with Swift specific content.\nUse **Keychain Services** for sensitive data (tokens, passwords, keys) — never \nUse environment variables or  files for build-time secrets\nNever hardcode secrets in source — dec",
      "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - \"**/*.swift\"\n  - \"**/Package.swift\"\n---\n# Swift Security\n\n> This file extends [common/security.md](../common/security.md) with Swift specific content.\n\n## Secret Management\n\n- Use **Keychain Services** for sensitive data (tokens, passwords, keys) — never `UserDefaults`\n- Use environment variables or `.xcconfig` files for build-time secrets\n- Never hardcode secrets in source — decompilation tools extract them trivially\n\n```swift\nlet apiKey = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment[\"API_KEY\"]\nguard let apiKey, !apiKey.isEmpty else {\n    fatalError(\"API_KEY not configured\")\n}\n```\n\n## Transport Security\n\n- App Transport Security (ATS) is enforced by default — do not disable it\n- Use certificate pinning for critical endpoints\n- Validate all server certificates\n\n## Input Validation\n\n- Sanitize all user input before display to prevent injection\n- Use `URL(string:)` with validation rather than force-unwrapping\n- Validate data from external sources (APIs, deep links, pasteboard) before processing\n",
      "renderedContent": "<hr>\n<h2>paths:\n  - &quot;<strong>/*.swift&quot;\n  - &quot;<\/strong>/Package.swift&quot;<\/h2>\n<h1>Swift Security<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p>This file extends <a href=\"../common/security.md\">common/security.md<\/a> with Swift specific content.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<h2>Secret Management<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Use <strong>Keychain Services<\/strong> for sensitive data (tokens, passwords, keys) — never <code>UserDefaults<\/code><\/li>\n<li>Use environment variables or <code>.xcconfig<\/code> files for build-time secrets<\/li>\n<li>Never hardcode secrets in source — decompilation tools extract them trivially<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<pre><code class=\"language-swift\">let apiKey = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment[&quot;API_KEY&quot;]\nguard let apiKey, !apiKey.isEmpty else {\n    fatalError(&quot;API_KEY not configured&quot;)\n}\n<\/code><\/pre>\n<h2>Transport Security<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>App Transport Security (ATS) is enforced by default — do not disable it<\/li>\n<li>Use certificate pinning for critical endpoints<\/li>\n<li>Validate all server certificates<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Input Validation<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li>Sanitize all user input before display to prevent injection<\/li>\n<li>Use <code>URL(string:)<\/code> with validation rather than force-unwrapping<\/li>\n<li>Validate data from external sources (APIs, deep links, pasteboard) before processing<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n"
    },
